exact_p_credit_static_review.result: The real-arithmetic IO certificate is valid under the stated frozen-plan preconditions; this is a static proof review, not an execution test or machine certification.
argument: The protected plan is legal, distinct-SPILL, retains q, and loads p; every returned victim larger than M-size(p)-size(q) is compulsory. Legal capacity implies no other such initial resident victim can remain, so f2 equals the compulsory write total.

If unprotected execution ends q service with both p and q resident, it must already write all compulsory victims plus its distinct initial q spill. Its IO therefore cannot beat the protected f2 plan after cancelling the common p read.
If p is absent at q service, it must have undergone an additional full-size SPILL after its own service. The unprotected branch also reloads q; thus extra p-write credit up to size(p)/W is justified.

Periodic preloading can avoid a q miss but cannot avoid its read and necessary spills. The protected frozen periodic path performs no IO when q is resident. The comparison cut is before q's own periodic callback.
implementation_contract_notes: The helper does not itself prove victim uniqueness, full plan feasibility, or exclusion of p/q. These properties come from the frozen plan implementation and caller. Do not reuse it as a validator for arbitrary action vectors.

The old guard is preserved as the first short-circuit OR operand. Only the newly accepted, forced-victim-certified p-credit region has this new argument. The inherited +1us/d-credit acceptance region is not all certified by it.
Zero-size targets, incompatible p+q, non-SPILL victims and non-forced victims are rejected by the helper. Signed deficit arithmetic remains within int64 under formal capacity limits.
Double comparison rounding, callback D, miss-penalty credit, unknown future operations and full Score remain outside the guarantee.
